articles.title: YOUR PRODUCT MAY ALREADY BE BROKEN
articles.summary:
They said “if it ain't broke, don't fix it” – but by the time you realize your UX is broken, it's already too late. That's because most UX problems aren't obvious [5] – they surface as hesitation, repeated clicks, and quiet drop-off, spread across tools that update on different timelines.

Datadog's guide [6] shows PMs how to gain true observability over user behavior, so they can detect friction earlier, respond while releases are still active, and prove business impact for every decision. You'll learn:

* Why timing (not access) is the real challenge. * The pulse, pain, and proof framework for organizing signals. * Three habits that separate good PMs from great ones.

articles.title: WHEN PRODUCT WORK OUTGROWS THE PLAN
articles.summary: When product work outgrows its original plan, PMs can use a Leadership Initiative Summary to reconnect tasks with customer value, build milestone plans, and present clear, actionable decisions to leadership.

articles.title: TECH FOR PRODUCT MANAGERS: HOW TECHNICAL YOU NEED TO BE IN 2026
articles.summary: PMs can build technical confidence via a four-level builder ladder starting with tools like Lovable and Claude Code. By testing on personal projects first, non-technical PMs can create internal prototypes without learning to code from scratch.

articles.title: THE ANSWER TO SLOP IS ACCOUNTABILITY
articles.summary: Software engineering often lacks accountability for low-quality AI output. Holding product managers directly responsible for software performance helps reduce subpar AI integrations.

articles.title: EMPOWERED, BUT…
articles.summary: Merging roles into AI-empowered "product engineers" risks creating a feature factory detached from strategy. PMs should prioritize business decisions and direct customer insight over speed.

5 WAYS YOU'RE MISUSING ICE SCORING

articles.title: PLANNING AN AI FEATURE PEOPLE WILL ACTUALLY USE
articles.summary: This practical framework plans AI features by targeting specific user friction points rather than deploying generic chatbots. Teams should map value against risk and write capability briefs before prototyping.

articles.title: WHEN THE BOSS STARTS SHIPPING: PRODUCT LEADERS, AI AND THE CODEBASE
articles.summary: When leaders use AI tools to ship code directly to production, it creates hidden tech debt. Establishing separate sandbox and production lanes ensures leadership follows standard testing processes.
